clauses.current_legal_basis: Held original order (22 FR 4632) read in full; every held later instrument is attached as a later event (EO 10979, EO 11085, EO 12014); the held current eCFR text of 5 CFR 451.203 (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) states that the Office of Personnel Management, in accordance with Executive Order 10717, as amended, reviews agency recommendations for the President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service and recommends recipients to the President; bounded searches current-law:usc (release point 119-121, edition through 2026-10-09: prints the order as a note to 5 U.S.C. 4504 with no ending statement), current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (5 machine hits; the held chain lists EO 10979, EO 11085 and EO 12014 and no other instrument) surfaced no ending of sections 1 and 2.
clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the honorary President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service (gold medal, ribbon and citation). It has no own-terms end and no instrument held deletes or replaces it. EO 11085 section 2(a) says the other sections of EO 10717 are amended conformably to that order but states no change to this wording, and EO 12014 deletes only sections 3 to 9. The held 5 CFR 451.203 still describes the Award under EO 10717 as amended. Operative on 2026-10-14.

clauses.reason: Section 2 provides that the Award is presented by the President to civilian officers or employees. EO 10979 (effective 1961-12-12) substituted a new section 2 (criteria for the best achievements having current impact, group-achievement and limit of generally five awards a year); under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, and the human reviewer should note that the substance of the section was rewritten. No later instrument ends it, EO 12014 did not delete section 2, and 5 CFR 451.203 still describes the Award. Operative on 2026-10-14 as amended.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 3 established the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board of five members. EO 12014 (signed 1977-10-19; no separate effective-date clause) abolished the Board and deleted sections 3 to 9 of EO 10717, so this command ended on that date; EO 12014 added new sections 3 and 4 placing the advisory function in the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, which is replacement text outside this original inventory. No earlier end is held (the Board continued: EO 11085 expanded it in 1963). The exact date reading is the signing date.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 4 fixed four-year terms for Board members; EO 11085 section 2(a) (1963-02-22) rewrote it to say members serve at the pleasure of the President, and EO 12014 (1977-10-19) deleted the section with the abolition of the Board. First end 1977-10-19 by deletion; the 1963 rewrite is a later event that kept the clause alive until then.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 5 (Board members serve without additional compensation; the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission is Executive Secretary and the Commission is requested to furnish staff) ended when EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Board and deleted section 5. No earlier end is held.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 6 (the Board advises and assists the President in selecting recipients) ended when EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Board and deleted section 6; the selection function reappears in new section 3 added by EO 12014, which is replacement text outside this inventory. No earlier end is held.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 7 (recommendations by agency heads to the Board) was rewritten by EO 10979 (1961-12-12) to let the Board prescribe the nomination method and require agency-head concurrence; the clause continued, amended, until EO 12014 (1977-10-19) deleted it. First end 1977-10-19.

clauses.mechanism: deleted by amendment and Board abolished
clauses.reason: Section 8 (the Board guided by section 304(b) and (c) of the Incentive Awards Act and criteria, with criteria paragraphs (a) and (b)) was rewritten by EO 10979 (1961-12-12) and continued, amended, until EO 12014 (1977-10-19) deleted it. First end 1977-10-19.

clauses.mechanism: own terms: effective-date clause exhausted on the date stated
clauses.reason: Section 9 provides that the order becomes effective on July 1, 1957. It is a spent effective-date clause: it was exhausted when the order took effect on 1957-07-01 (own terms), and EO 12014 later deleted it. First end 1957-07-01 under the order's own terms; the exclusive reading (ends when that day begins) is the alternative.

research_rationale:
Whole-lifecycle YES claim for EO 10717 (The President's Award for Distinguished Federal Civilian Service, June 27, 1957, 22 FR 4632), read in full from the held Federal Register text after correcting the packet inventory (which listed only parts of sections 3 and 9) to the nine original sections. Sections 1 and 2 (the Award and its presentation by the President) remain operative: EO 10979 (1961-12-12) rewrote section 2 and EO 11085 (1963-02-22) amended section 4 and the others conformably, and EO 12014 (1977-10-19) abolished the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board and deleted sections 3 to 9, adding new sections 3 and 4 that vest the advisory and nomination functions in the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission. EO 12107 (1978-12-28, effective 1979-01-01) then substituted the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in the added text; it touches none of the original sections inventoried here. Sections 3 to 8 ended on 1977-10-19 by deletion and section 9, a spent effective-date clause, ended on 1957-07-01 under the order's own terms. The held 5 CFR 451.203 shows the Award still operating under EO 10717 as amended (eCFR as of 2026-10-14). The U.S. Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; that limit is stated, not filled.
